summary: Learn to govern AI agents, set guardrails, and monitor workplace automation with practical templates and hands-on exercises.
lede: Managing AI agents in the workplace means defining agent roles, setting guardrails, validating outputs, and establishing human oversight so automated work remains accurate, secure, and aligned with business needs. This course helps you structure prompt governance, task decomposition, exception handling, and disciplined data use across workflows that may involve customers, finance, compliance, or internal service delivery. You will practise creating an AI agent use-case canvas, guardrails checklist, role charter, review rubric, monitoring dashboard concept, escalation workflow, and deployment readiness brief. The course also introduces multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation patterns, and operational observability, helping you approve use cases, supervise outputs, and report progress within real workplace constraints.
audienceIntro: This course is built for people who need to supervise AI agents, approve automation use cases, and keep output quality under control inside day-to-day operations.
audience: Customer Operations Managers using agents for triage
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of business processes, basic data handling, and common workplace software such as spreadsheets and collaborative document tools. No programming is required for completion, although familiarity with AI assistants or automation tools will help you move faster through the exercises. The course is best suited to intermediate-level professionals who already make or influence workflow, policy, or quality decisions. Advanced topics such as agent orchestration and monitoring are taught at an operational application level, with hands-on design exercises rather than software development.
topics: Generative AI at work & AI copilots
